review: 2:1–2:2 כִּי בְדָבָר זֶה בְּחַרְתָּנוּ / מֵעוֹלָם וָקֶדֶם — 'for in this matter You chose us, from eternity and of old'; Hebrew makes the 'in His person' explicit as בְדָבָר זֶה ('in this one') rather than repeating בְּאִישׁ ('in a man').
2:3 מְלֹא הָעִתִּים — 'the fullness of the times' (Eph 1:10); the Arabic مِلْءِ الزَّمَان is that phrase, and the plural הָעִתִּים is deliberate.
3:2–3:3 וַיַּשְׁלֵם ... וַיָּשֶׁב — two wayyiqtol verbs, because the Arabic قَضَى / أَكْمَلَ / رَدَّ is a narrative sequence and Hebrew narrative tense is the right register here.
3:3 כְּבוֹדְךָ הַגָּזוּל — 'Your stolen glory'; גָּזוּל is the passive participle of גזל (theft), which is the biblical word for what Adam lost.
4:1–4:2 וְאַתָּה הַחַנּוּן / שַׂמְתָּהוּ עַל־כֹּל — the Arabic أَيُّهَا الْحَنُون is a vocative; Hebrew keeps the article as a vocative of address, as in the psalms.
